sessions.question: How did OCBC's NPL ratio change from 2024 to 2025?
sessions.answer:
**OCBC's Group NPL ratio was unchanged at 0.9% from 2024 to 2025 — no change (0.0 percentage points).**

- 2025: 0.9%; 2024: 0.9% — key financial ratios table (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96)
- The 2024 annual report confirms the same figures: 2024 0.9% vs 2023 1.0% (ocbc-group_ar_2024_en, physical page 98, printed page 96), i.e. the ratio had already fallen 0.1 pp in 2024 and then held flat in 2025.

Supporting detail from the MD&A "Allowances and Asset Quality" section (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 100, printed page 98):
- Total NPAs were $3.24 billion as at 31 December 2025, up 13% from a year ago
- "NPL ratio remained unchanged at 0.9%, and total NPA coverage stood at 151%"
- Total allowances were 4% lower at $665 million; credit costs declined to 17 basis points from 19 basis points a year ago

Fact-layer note: the 0.9% for 2025 comes from a single source (the 2025 annual report key ratios table), while 2024 and 2023 are marked "agreed" across two sources; no restatements are recorded.

Gap: the Chinese edition (ocbc-group_ar_2025_zh) exists but was not searched here; the figures above come from the full English edition.

sessions.question: What was OCBC's net profit growth in 2025 compared with 2024?
sessions.answer:
**OCBC's net profit declined slightly in 2025.**

- FY2025 net profit attributable to equity holders: **$7,422 million**, vs **$7,587 million** in FY2024 — a decrease of **$165 million, or 2%** (the report states "(2)" % year on year) (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96).
- The MD&A narrative confirms: "Group net profit of $7.42 billion for 2025 was 2% below the record $7.59 billion in the previous year" (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 99, printed page 97).
- The five-year summary confirms the same figures: 2024 $7,587m, 2025 $7,422m (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 4, printed page 2).

Supporting context from the same MD&A overview:
- Profit before income tax rose 2% to a record $9.12 billion, and total income was a record $14.6 billion (up 1%, with non-interest income +16% offsetting net interest income -6%); tax expense was 27% higher mainly due to higher profit contribution from higher-tax jurisdictions and BEPS Pillar Two top-up tax (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 99, printed page 97).
- Cash basis net profit attributable to equity holders was $7,443m, down 3% from $7,646m (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96).
- Return on equity fell to 12.6% from 13.7%; basic earnings per share $1.63 vs $1.67 (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96).

Fact status: the net profit figures are "agreed" across multiple sources (2025 figure from 2 sources: the 2025 five-year summary and MD&A overview table); no restatements for 2024/2025 (the 2022 figure was restated for SFRS(I) 17, which does not affect this comparison). The "-2%" is the figure as stated in the report; the derived change is -$165m / -2.17% from $7,587m to $7,422m.

Gap note: Chinese-language editions exist (ocbc-group_ar_2023_zh, ocbc-group_ar_2024_zh, ocbc-group_ar_2025_zh) but were not searched here; all figures above come from the English 2025 annual report.

sessions.question: What was OCBC's liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) in 2025?
sessions.answer:
**OCBC's 2025 liquidity coverage ratios (as at 31 December 2025, reported on the average LCR for the year):**

| Ratio | 2025 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Singapore dollar liquidity coverage ratio | 294% | 299% |
| All-currency liquidity coverage ratio | 138% | 141% |

Source: "Key Financial Ratios" table, MD&A Overview (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96).

Notes and caveats:
- The Group's LCRs are computed based on MAS Notice 649 and reported based on the average LCR for the respective years (footnote 8, same page).
- The Group also reported a net stable funding ratio of 114% in 2025 (113% in 2024), computed based on MAS Notice 652 (same page).
- These are Group-level figures from the English 2025 Annual Report. Detailed MAS Notice 651 LCR disclosures are not in the annual report itself; they are in the Stand-alone Pillar 3 Disclosures Report published on OCBC's investor relations website (Pillar 3 Disclosures section, ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 79, printed page 77).
- The metric table for LCR had no machine-extracted fact series available (the fact layer covers only ~15 core metrics), so the values above come from reading the source table directly; no prior-year restatement was indicated.

sessions.question: What was OCBC's return on equity (ROE) in 2025?
sessions.answer:
**OCBC's return on equity (ROE) in 2025 was 12.6%.**

Details:

- **12.6%** for FY2025, down from **13.7%** in 2024 — a decline of 1.1 percentage points (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96; MD&A "Overview", Key Financial Ratios table).
- The MD&A narrative states: "The Group's return on equity was lower at 12.6%, while earnings per share was $1.63" (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 99, printed page 97).
- The Group Five-Year Summary confirms the same figure: ROE of 9.6% (2021), 11.1% (2022), 13.7% (2023), 13.7% (2024), 12.6% (2025) (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 4, printed page 2).
- The Chairman's Reflections also states ROE "remained resilient at 12.6%" (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 9, printed page 7 — page located via search but not read, so this wording is not independently verified).

Definition footnote: ROE is calculated based on net profit less distributions on other equity instruments paid and estimated to be due at the end of the financial year; other equity instruments and non-controlling interests are excluded from the computation (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 98, printed page 96).

Fact status: multiple sources agree (2 sources for the 2025 value, no restatement for 2025). Note one gap in the data: the 2022 figure is flagged as restated (SFRS(I) 17 adoption) in the 2025 report, and the report containing the original 2022 figure is not in the store, so no original value is available.

sessions.question: 华侨银行2025年的资本充足率（CET1）是多少？
sessions.answer:
**OCBC Group's CET1 capital adequacy ratio for 2025 was 16.9%.**

Details (as at 31 December 2025, Group level):

| Ratio | 2025 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) | 16.9% | 17.1% |
| Tier 1 | 17.6% | 17.8% |
| Total | 19.4% | 19.7% |

- Five-year summary: CET1 15.5% (2021), 15.2% (2022, restated), 15.9% (2023), 17.1% (2024), 16.9% (2025) (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 4, printed page 2).
- MD&A: "The Group remained strongly capitalised, with a CET1 CAR of 16.9%, and Tier 1 and Total CAR of 17.6% and 19.4% respectively. These ratios were well above the regulatory minima of 6.5%, 8% and 10%, respectively, for 2025." (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 110, printed page 108).
- Also stated: the Group's CET1 CAR based on fully phased-in final Basel III reforms was 15.1% (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 110, printed page 108).
- Fact status: "agreed" (multiple sources agree); the 2025 figure is down 0.2 percentage points year on year. Note: 2025 and 2024 ratios were computed under MAS' final Basel III reforms, phased in between 1 July 2024 and 1 January 2029, so they are not directly comparable with pre-2024 fully phased-in Basel III figures (ocbc-group_ar_2025_en, physical page 4, printed page 2).
